another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I'm ready to help you determine your Child Benefit eligibility. Let me start by asking about your child.

**First, I need to know about your child's age:**

Is your child:
- **Under 16 years old?**
- **Between 16-19 years old?**
- **20 years old or over?**

Please tell me how old your child is, and if you have more than one child you're asking about, please let me know about all of them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 19 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son Alex who is 19 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 19 (which falls in the 16-19 age category), there are additional requirements for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to understand Alex's current education or training status.

**Is Alex currently:**

1. **In approved education or training** (such as full-time non-advanced education at school, college, or approved training)?

2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks)?

3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

Could you let me know which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is currently in education - he's studying for his A-levels at college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is studying for his A-levels at college, which is approved education. Let me check the next requirement regarding the level of education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! A-levels are definitely approved non-advanced education, which is good news. Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's education and circumstances:

**1. Is Alex studying full-time** (at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)?

**2. Is this education funded by an employer or linked to a guaranteed job with an employer?** (This would exclude eligibility, but college A-levels typically aren't employer-funded)

**3. Is Alex married or in a civil partnership?** (If so, there's an additional requirement about financial dependency)

Please let me know about these points.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's studying full-time at college - definitely more than 12 hours a week of classes and coursework. No, it's not funded by an employer - it's just regular college. And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move forward with this information. Alex is in approved full-time education (A-levels), it's not employer-funded, and he's not married. This all meets the education requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

Excellent! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week** (or not in paid work at all)?

For Child Benefit purposes, children aged 16+ who work 24 hours or more per week are not considered qualifying children.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex does work - he has a full-time job at the supermarket alongside his college studies. So yes, he's working 24 hours or more per week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important detail. Alex is working 24 hours or more per week at the supermarket alongside his college studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I need to provide you with the eligibility decision based on Alex's circumstances.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on Alex's circumstances, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit** for him.

## Why Alex doesn't qualify:

While Alex is doing everything right by studying full-time for his A-levels (which is approved education), the issue is that he's working 24 or more hours per week at the supermarket. Under UK Child Benefit rules, **children aged 16 or over who work 24 hours or more per week are not considered qualifying children** for Child Benefit purposes, even if they're also in approved education.

## What this means:

- Child Benefit stops when a child aged 16+ starts paid work for 24 or more hours per week
- This applies even though Alex is still in approved education

## Important to know:

**If Alex's circumstances change** - for example, if he reduces his working hours to less than 24 hours per week while continuing his studies - you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. In that case, you could make a new claim or inform HMRC of the change.

I understand this may be disappointing, especially since Alex is working hard both at college and at his job. If you have any questions or if his circumstances change in the future, please don't hesitate to reach out.
